sections.title: Concept Overview
sections.content: In Level 2, questions on confusing words are slightly more complex. A single sentence may contain two blanks, or grammar may also need to be considered to select the correct word. In such questions, it is important to pay attention to both the meaning and the part of speech.

sections.title: Double Fillers (Pair Selection)
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence and understand its main meaning. Step 2: Identify the context by looking at the words around both blanks. Step 3: Compare the meanings of the confusing word pairs given in the options. Step 4: Choose the pair that fits both blanks logically and grammatically. Example: 'She accepted the job because the salary was very ___, and the office was ___ her house.' Correct pair: 'attractive / near'.

sections.title: Parts of Speech Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Look at the words before and after the blank. Step 2: Decide whether the blank requires a noun, verb, adjective, or adverb. Step 3: Choose the word from the options that fits grammatically. Example: 'He will ___ the prize tomorrow.' Here a verb is required, so 'receive' is correct.

sections.title: Meaning vs Grammar Check
sections.content: Step 1: First eliminate options that are grammatically incorrect. Step 2: From the remaining words, match the meaning according to the context. Step 3: Read the entire sentence again to check if it sounds natural. Example: 'The teacher asked the students to ___ the lesson carefully.' Correct word: 'revise'.

sections.title: Common Confusing Word Pairs
sections.content: Some common confusing pairs are: affect/effect, advice/advise, accept/except, compliment/complement, stationary/stationery, principle/principal. These words have different meanings and grammatical roles.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing a word only based on pronunciation. 2. Ignoring the grammatical requirement. 3. Looking at both blanks separately and forgetting the pair logic.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In double filler questions, you must choose the correct pair of words for both blanks. To do this, it is necessary to use context, grammar, and word meaning together.

tricks.title: POS Check Trick
tricks.explanation: If an article or adjective appears before the blank, a noun is usually required.

tricks.title: Verb Indicator Trick
tricks.explanation: After modal verbs (can, will, should), the base form of the verb is used.

tricks.title: Meaning Pair Check
tricks.explanation: In double blanks, the meanings of both words must match the sentence context.
tricks.example: He bought new stationery to keep his desk stationary.

tricks.title: Affect vs Effect Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Affect' is usually a verb, while 'Effect' is generally a noun.

tricks.title: Advice vs Advise Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Advice' is a noun, while 'Advise' is a verb.
tricks.example: She advised him to follow good advice.

tricks.title: Accept vs Except Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Accept' means to receive, while 'Except' means excluding.
tricks.example: Everyone accepted the rule except John.

tricks.title: Context Confirmation Trick
tricks.explanation: After choosing the answer, read the entire sentence again.
tricks.example: The sentence should sound natural and logical.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: First remove grammatically incorrect options, then choose the correct one based on meaning.
tricks.example: If a verb is required, eliminate options that are nouns.
